$comment: Record schema for the analysis layer. Nothing here reads a browser.
Collection is a separate problem with separate obstacles; this layer consumes
whatever you already have, in whatever shape, and refuses to invent numbers.
THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST, stated first because it invalidates the most
ABSOLUTE engagement is confounded by audience size. 1,000 likes from 10,000
followers is a WORSE result than 300 likes from 1,000 followers, by a factor of
three. Ranking notes or creators by raw like count therefore measures mostly
If follower counts are absent, every rate-like metric here is reported as
unavailable rather than approximated. The analyzer will not silently fall back
to absolute numbers under a rate-flavoured name.
Minimum viable data for a useful analysis is: note title, author, like count,
and follower count. Everything else is enrichment.

optional.note_id: platform id, for dedupe across exports
optional.title: note title or first line of caption
optional.published_at: ISO date or date-time. Enables cadence and timing analysis
optional.collects: integer. Enables collect-rate, which on this platform often separates savers from likers
optional.topics: array of strings. Enables topic/engagement association
optional.captured_at: ISO date. When you observed it. Lets the analyzer say how stale the data is

note.unknowns: Every optional field may be absent or null. Absence is recorded, never imputed.

authorSnapshot.$comment: Follower counts over time. Without at least two of these for an author, no growth curve is possible.

optional.likes_total: aggregate likes across their notes at that date
optional.note_count: how many notes had been published by that date

parsing.counts: Accepts 1.2万 and 3.8k and 1,234 and '1.2w'. Strips thousands separators. Returns null for '', '-', '赞' and anything unparseable, and records the cell rather than coercing it to 0.
parsing.$comment: Coercing an unreadable cell to 0 is the most damaging thing an importer can do: it pulls a mean down and nobody notices.
parsing.dates: Accepts YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY年M月D日, and an ISO date-time. Returns null rather than guessing when ambiguous.

magnitude.$comment: 千 was missing from this table until the CSV importer was run against a hand-entered sheet containing 9.1千. The regex matched 9.1 with no unit and returned 9, so a follower count of 9,100 became 9 and the engagement rate came out at 48507%. Any magnitude unit a person might type belongs here.

sanity.$comment: Values that survive parsing but are implausible indicate a parse or unit error upstream. The analyzer reports these rather than computing on them.
sanity.followers_below_likes: A note with more likes than the author has followers usually means the follower column was mis-parsed. Flagged, not corrected.
sanity.rate_over_1: An interaction rate above 100% is possible on this platform when a note travels beyond the following, but above ~300% usually means a bad denominator.
